encounters.cc: Recurrent epistaxis requiring increased medical attention over the past year

lines: Recurrent epistaxis requiring increased medical attention over the past year
History of recurrent nosebleeds since childhood.
She reports that the nosebleeds have increased in frequency over the past year, often occurring several times a week and sometimes requiring medical attention to control.
She also mentions occasional blood-tinged sputum but denies any cough or shortness of breath.
- Dilatation and curettage for spontaneous abortion at 10 weeks gestation (age 32)
- Emergency cesarean delivery for fetal distress (age 32)
- Mesalamine 1.2 g PO three times daily
- Prednisone 10 mg PO daily (chronic low-dose with intermittent tapers for flares)
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs every 4-6 hours PRN for wheezing
Her family history is significant for similar symptoms in her father and a cousin.
On examination, you note several small red-to-purple lesions on her lips and oral mucosa.
Auscultation of the chest reveals no abnormalities.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of intermittent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and recent onset of malodorous vaginal discharge with passage of flatus per vagina

lines: Six-month history of intermittent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and recent onset of malodorous vaginal discharge with passage of flatus per vagina
The patient with Crohn's disease, SLE, and HHT returns following January 2020 Pulmonology encounter with a 6-month history of intermittent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and unintentional weight loss.
She also describes recent onset of malodorous, tan vaginal discharge with occasional passage of flatus per vagina.
Crohn's disease diagnosed 8 years ago, which has been managed with mesalamine and intermittent corticosteroids.
- Dilatation and curettage for spontaneous abortion at 10 weeks gestation (age 32)
- Emergency cesarean delivery for fetal distress (age 32)
- Mesalamine 1.2 g PO three times daily
- Prednisone 10 mg PO daily (chronic low-dose with intermittent tapers for flares)
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs every 4-6 hours PRN for wheezing
On physical examination, she is afebrile, and her abdominal exam reveals tenderness in the right lower quadrant without rebound or guarding.
Pelvic examination shows a small lesion on the posterior vaginal wall.
- Stool cultures: No pathogenic bacteria, ova, or parasites detected

encounters.cc: Generalized tonic-clonic seizure with several months of preceding headaches and photosensitive malar rash

lines: Generalized tonic-clonic seizure with several months of preceding headaches and photosensitive malar rash
The patient with systemic lupus erythematosus, Crohn's disease, and recent gastroenterology follow-up presents to the emergency department.
Her boyfriend reports intermittent headaches, fatigue, and a malar rash that worsens with sun exposure over the past few months.
Her medical history is significant for mild intermittent asthma and one episode of unexplained thrombocytopenia last year.
- Dilatation and curettage for spontaneous abortion at 10 weeks gestation (age 32)
- Emergency cesarean delivery for fetal distress (age 32)
- Mesalamine 1.2 g PO three times daily
- Prednisone 10 mg PO daily (chronic low-dose with intermittent tapers for flares)
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs every 4-6 hours PRN for wheezing
Her temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, and heart rate is 88/min.
On examination, she is postictal but arousable.
A malar rash is noted across her cheeks and bridge of her nose.
- Urinalysis: 2+ protein, 5-10 red blood cells/high power field

encounters.cc: Shortness of breath and heavy intermittent vaginal bleeding three months after spontaneous abortion

lines: Shortness of breath and heavy intermittent vaginal bleeding three months after spontaneous abortion

The patient is a 35-year-old female with Crohn's disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, and hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, previously evaluated for rectovaginal fistula and neuropsychiatric SLE.
She presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath and intermittent vaginal bleeding for the past two weeks.
She reports that the bleeding is irregular and heavier than her normal menstrual periods.
She had a spontaneous abortion 3 months ago at 10 weeks gestation, which was followed by a dilation and curettage procedure.
- Systemic Lupus Erythematosus with Central Nervous System Involvement (Neuropsychiatric SLE) (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Dilatation and curettage for spontaneous abortion at 10 weeks gestation (age 32)
- Emergency cesarean delivery for fetal distress (age 32)
- Mesalamine 1.2 g PO three times daily
- Prednisone 10 mg PO daily (chronic low-dose with intermittent tapers for flares)
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs every 4-6 hours PRN for wheezing
Her vital signs are as follows: blood pressure 130/85 mmHg, heart rate 102 beats per minute, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation 94% on room air.
On physical examination, her uterus is palpably enlarged.
Auscultation of the lungs reveals diffuse rales.
A chest x-ray shows multiple bilateral pulmonary infiltrates.

encounters.cc: Bilateral breast pain and swelling four days after spontaneous vaginal delivery with infant feeding difficulties

lines: Bilateral breast pain and swelling four days after spontaneous vaginal delivery with infant feeding difficulties

This 35-year-old patient with Crohn's disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, and recent history of choriocarcinoma presents to the obstetrics clinic four days following spontaneous vaginal delivery with complaints of bilateral breast pain and swelling.
She reports that she has been trying to breastfeed her newborn, but the baby seems to have difficulty latching on, and she is not sure if the baby is getting enough milk.
She denies any fever, nipple discharge, or red streaks on her breasts.
She is eager to continue breastfeeding and asks for advice on how to alleviate her discomfort.
- Systemic Lupus Erythematosus with Central Nervous System Involvement (Neuropsychiatric SLE) (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Dilatation and curettage for spontaneous abortion at 10 weeks gestation (age 32)
- Emergency cesarean delivery for fetal distress (age 32)
- Mesalamine 1.2 g PO three times daily
- Prednisone 10 mg PO daily (chronic low-dose with intermittent tapers for flares)
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs every 4-6 hours PRN for wheezing
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
On examination, her breasts are symmetrically enlarged, firm, and tender to palpation.
There is no skin discoloration, and the nipples are intact without cracks or fissures.

encounters.cc: Painful vesicular lesions on right breast developing during exclusive breastfeeding four weeks postpartum

lines: Painful vesicular lesions on right breast developing during exclusive breastfeeding four weeks postpartum

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with Crohn's disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, and mild intermittent asthma who returns for a routine postpartum visit with her 4-week-old infant four weeks following spontaneous vaginal delivery and recent choriocarcinoma.
She presents following her recent evaluation for postpartum breast engorgement.
She reports that she has been exclusively breastfeeding and is concerned because she has developed painful vesicular lesions on her right breast over the past two days.
She denies any fever, chills, or flu-like symptoms.
The infant appears well and is gaining weight appropriately.
She has not received any recent vaccinations or been exposed to any sick contacts.
- Systemic Lupus Erythematosus with Central Nervous System Involvement (Neuropsychiatric SLE) (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Dilatation and curettage for spontaneous abortion at 10 weeks gestation (age 32)
- Emergency cesarean delivery for fetal distress (age 32)
- Mesalamine 1.2 g PO three times daily
- Prednisone 10 mg PO daily (chronic low-dose with intermittent tapers for flares)
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs every 4-6 hours PRN for wheezing
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
On examination, the mother has multiple clustered vesicles on an erythematous base localized to the areola of the right breast.
There are no similar lesions elsewhere on her body
Complete blood count: Within normal limits

encounters.cc: Fever of 38.5°C with incisional pain and erythema on postoperative day three following emergency cesarean delivery

lines: Fever of 38.5°C with incisional pain and erythema on postoperative day three following emergency cesarean delivery
The patient with Crohn's disease and systemic lupus erythematosus presents three days after emergency cesarean delivery for fetal distress with pain and redness around her surgical incision.
- Systemic Lupus Erythematosus with Central Nervous System Involvement (Neuropsychiatric SLE) (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Dilatation and curettage for spontaneous abortion at 10 weeks gestation (age 32)
- Emergency cesarean delivery for fetal distress (age 32)
- Mesalamine 1.2 g PO three times daily
- Prednisone 10 mg PO daily (chronic low-dose with intermittent tapers for flares)
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs every 4-6 hours PRN for wheezing
On examination, the lower segment cesarean section incision is erythematous and indurated with mild purulent discharge.
Her white blood cell count is 14,000/µL, and her C-reactive protein is elevated.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset right-sided weakness and aphasia with preceding chest discomfort and lightheadedness six months postpartum

lines: Sudden-onset right-sided weakness and aphasia with preceding chest discomfort and lightheadedness six months postpartum
The patient with systemic lupus erythematosus and prior choriocarcinoma presents six months postpartum.
She has since felt generally well, though she recently noted episodes of lightheadedness and intermittent dull chest discomfort.
She has not had follow-up care since delivery.
- Systemic Lupus Erythematosus with Central Nervous System Involvement (Neuropsychiatric SLE) (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Superficial surgical site infection (cellulitis) following cesarean delivery (diagnosed 2024-01-15)
She has no known history of hypertension, diabetes, or stroke.
Her only recent medical event was a spontaneous vaginal delivery 3 months ago.
- Dilatation and curettage for spontaneous abortion at 10 weeks gestation (age 32)
- Emergency cesarean delivery for fetal distress (age 32)
- Mesalamine 1.2 g PO three times daily
- Prednisone 10 mg PO daily (chronic low-dose with intermittent tapers for flares)
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs every 4-6 hours PRN for wheezing
She denies illicit drug use, recent travel, or trauma.
Temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg, and pulse is 92/min.
On examination, she is alert but has expressive aphasia, right upper and lower extremity hemiparesis, and a right facial droop.
Cardiopulmonary and abdominal exams are unremarkable.
A CT scan of the head shows a hemorrhagic lesion in the left parietal lobe.
CT angiography of the chest reveals multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules.
